_comment: Declarative execution pipeline. Stage commands use placeholders resolved from .agentry/project/stack.md during interactive onboarding (see _init-prompt.md Phase B). The deterministic hooks (tools/pipeline/*.py) read this file; the model never decides a transition.
_stop_hook_repeat_ceiling_comment: Read by tools/pipeline/stop_gate.py block(). How many CONSECUTIVE blocks may carry the SAME reason before the hook stops repeating it: it parks the run the reason names, or - when the reason names no run - escalates once to the CEO and then goes quiet about that sentence. Independent of continuation_ceiling, which is per run and per stage; this one is per reason and survives stage transitions, so it catches the loops no per-branch budget can see. Armed only while the hook payload's stop_hook_active is true, so every demand is uttered at least once per turn whatever its history. Three by CEO decision RQ-7: two identical blocks are a legitimate retry. A missing or unreadable key falls back to 3; a value below 1 disables the backstop and every branch reports exactly as it did before it existed, which is the fail-open direction NFR-4 wants - losing a bound is recoverable, losing the report is the silent halt.

workflow._comment: What kind of project this is, read by tools/pipeline/pretool_gate.py. mode 'pr' (DEFAULT when absent) is the collaborative shape: nothing commits on the trunk, the branch is pushed and a human opens the pull request. mode 'solo' is the single-author shape: there is no second party to review or merge, so a LOCAL `git merge` of an approved task branch into the trunk is allowed - the task must still match <type>/task-NNNN, have a row in run.db, and carry an approved commit checkpoint, because those guard against merging unreviewed work rather than against working alone. Pushing to a protected branch is refused in BOTH modes, with one exception: in 'solo' mode the trunk itself may be published by a push the CEO approved in chat and the orchestrator recorded with approve.py --trunk-push, and that approval covers exactly ONE push (the push consumes the marker). No approvals level ever grants it, and an unattended session is refused it regardless. push_needs_approval is independent of the mode (default true): working alone says nothing about whether an unattended run may write to the remote. See .claude/rules/git-workflow.md.

memory._comment: Post-task memory review gate (tools/memory/update.py): every done task above baseline must be distilled into .agentry/memory/ (lessons/patterns/codebase rows) and stamped before the next task starts. Enforced by advance.py (registration refusal, beside the handoff gate - task-0066 added it, before which this line named an enforcer that did not exist) and stop_gate.py (blocks the stop while the debt stands, whatever is in flight). baseline semantics match handoff.baseline; '' = every done task covered. enabled=false disables the gate.
memory._comment_inject: Retrieval caps read by tools/memory/inject.py (contract C-5, task-0011), separate from the gate keys above. inject_budget_bytes caps the whole injected BLOCK in UTF-8 bytes - the text inside the hook's JSON envelope, not the emitted object, whose scaffolding and escaping sit outside the budget (task-0081); rows are dropped from the tail until the block fits, and the head line then reports 'N of M matching row(s) (byte budget)'. inject_row_chars caps each single row in characters before that trimming starts, appending ' ...'. Both fall back to their defaults (3800 / 700) when the key is missing, is not an integer, or is below 1 - the block is still emitted, per NFR-4. A small positive value is honoured as written; the last row is never dropped, so no setting here can silence injection. The third knob, how many rows are queried, is per-matcher: inject.py --limit in .claude/settings.json.

orchestrator_gate._comment: Hard gate on the MAIN THREAD (orchestrator): Edit/Write and shell file-writes are denied outside .claude/, .agentry/, docs/, README*, root CLAUDE.md. The orchestrator only formalizes tasks, delegates, verifies and synthesizes - it never authors code. Subagent tool calls are exempt (agent_gate.py profiles govern them). extra_allow: repo-relative globs to whitelist per project (e.g. "CHANGELOG.md"). enabled=false disables the gate.

gates._comment: Stack-specific denials read by tools/pipeline/{pretool_gate,agent_gate}.py. Filled during onboarding (see _init-prompt.md Phase B) from the detected language/framework so the gate CODE stays language-agnostic. Empty array / false / '' disables that gate. Generic gates (branch base+naming, AI-attribution in commits, em/en dash, writes under ~/.claude) need no config and always run.

handoff._comment: Forced context-absorption chain: before any NEW task registers, every done task with id above baseline must have a valid doc in dir. The doc is written by the NEXT task's assignee in its own words. baseline: '' for a fresh project (every done task covered); when adopting mid-project, set it at onboarding to the highest pre-existing done task id (those are grandfathered). Enforced by advance.py (registration refusal), stop_gate.py (start-next-task block) and pretool_gate.py (hard_edit_gate code-edit freeze). Tools: handoff.py --check / --for / --inject / --waive (waive is orchestrator-only, CEO approval required).
handoff._size_comment: max_total_bytes: the cap on ONE handoff doc, in raw file bytes (os.path.getsize), checked in validate_handoff beside the two thin-checks above. Affordable because --inject sends only the newest doc in full and the rest as index lines. inject_budget_bytes: the ceiling on the WHOLE injected block, the same idea as memory.inject_budget_bytes and failing open the same way. 7168 = one cap-compliant document (6144) plus the head, the path line and about nine index lines; max_total_bytes alone does not bound the block, because exempt docs are not exempt from injection and the index grows by about 100 bytes per completed task forever. Over budget the oldest index lines are dropped first and the newest document is truncated only after the index is gone, with a note naming its path. That order was inverted after measuring the other one: at 7168 it cut 1785 bytes out of the newest document while all 2526 bytes of index survived, which contradicts the block's own header, 'newest in full'. max_bytes_exempt: task ids the cap does not apply to, empty in a fresh project. It is a LIST rather than a numeric baseline because task ids are not chronological: measured in the Agentry workspace on 2026-09-15, the 18 documents already over the cap ran from task-0004 to task-0081 while the next one to be written was task-0016, so no threshold separates already-written from written-from-now-on. Adopting mid-project with oversized docs: list them here rather than trimming them. thread_max_bytes: the cap on an epic thread document, .agentry/tasks/epics/<epic-id>-thread.md, whose sections are 'Where the chain stands', 'What is decided' and 'What remains'; reported by handoff.py --check only and never by the registration path, so an oversized thread doc cannot block a task from starting. Each cap fails open on its own: absent, null, non-integer or non-positive means that cap is not enforced, because handoff.py is read by three hooks and a cap that rejected everything would refuse every registration and freeze every edit.

supervisor._comment: External supervisor (tools/pipeline/supervisor.py) - a process with its own clock, started DETACHED by the SessionStart hook (supervisor.py --ensure-running) and a singleton per lane, because a watcher that dies with the session cannot report that session's death. Stop it with supervisor.py --stop. It polls run.db plus the task folders, classifies every in-flight run HEALTHY / STALLED / LOOPING / DEAD from observed facts, relaunches STALLED and DEAD work as a headless session, and parks LOOPING work blocked. LOOPING is NEVER relaunched and there is no key here that can change that. stall_seconds: no change to the STAGE for this long, with no other evidence, is a stall (keep it above a slow exit gate - advance.py's own gate timeout is 900s). There is deliberately no loop_ticks key: task-0067 measured that reading firing on ordinary work (a 60s turn cycle parked a live task in three minutes) and deleted it, leaving the pipeline's own continuation_ceiling as the loop budget. idle_exit_polls: consecutive polls with nothing in flight after which the daemon exits and releases its lock (0 never exits). spawn_cmd: argv, never a shell string; placeholders {task} {stage} {prompt}. Its --permission-mode bypassPermissions is load-bearing, not decoration: a headless session has nobody to answer a permission prompt, so without it every tool call is auto-denied and the relaunch does nothing (task-0090); the hooks, not the prompt dialog, are what restrain a spawned session. Both caps are hard - exceeding either stops the supervisor and notifies. enabled=false makes it exit without looking, and makes the SessionStart hook a no-op.

build._comment: Implementation. Drives a task from code to a pushed branch. Merging into the main branch is always the CEO's, never the agent's.

stages.name: test
stages._comment: ui_evidence: true appends 'python .claude/tools/pipeline/ui_evidence.py --task {task}' to the exit gate at onboarding, so UI-touching tasks require real-browser evidence in .agentry/state/evidence/<task>.json. Set false for API-only projects.

stages.name: ready
stages._comment: auto_approve: checkpoints listed here (e.g. ["commit"] or ["commit", "push"]) are approved by advance.py itself - no CEO parking. Empty = both approvals stay manual. Decide at onboarding Phase B; changing it later is a CEO decision.

plan._comment: Design. Turns a request into an approved plan, a spec and task files sitting in tasks/backlog/. Writes documents, never product code.
plan._editing_stages_comment: Every stage an AGENT owns and the conveyor must drive to an exit gate. This key was [] until task-0020, on the reading that a planning stage writes documents rather than code and so serializes against nothing - which is false twice over: those documents are files in this repository's working tree, and stop_gate.decide() uses the set to decide what is IN FLIGHT, not what is compiled. Empty meant a plan run mid-flight matched no branch of the run loop, so nothing drove it and the next backlog task was started on top of it. `approval` is excluded because the CEO owns it, not an agent; `done` is excluded as terminal. `plan-review` IS included for the same reason build's `review` is: read-only for the reviewer does not mean the run has let go of its branch. `approval` is protected by being a checkpoint stage rather than by being absent from this list: state.checkpoint_stages() reads both the `checkpoint` and `checkpoints` spellings, so the Stop hook neither drives it nor treats its tree as free. Do NOT normalise `checkpoint` to `checkpoints` here as a cleanup - advance.stage_checkpoints() reads the plural and filters to commit/push, so renaming the key would change what advance.py does to this stage without giving the flow a real checkpoint. KNOWN GAP, follow-up task filed: the plan flow still has no checkpoint of its own - no run.db column, no advance.py branch - and an absent `exit_gate` is measured to return configured=true AND passed=true, so a hand-run advance.py still walks `approval` to `breakdown`. What task-0020 closed is the automatic half: nothing instructs anyone to do that every stop any more.

stages.name: formalize
stages._comment: Write the problem statement: what hurts, scope, non-goals, open questions. Parks on the CEO until the questions are answered - that information exists nowhere else.

stages.name: plan-review
stages._comment: Read-only review of the plan itself. Critical and High findings must be closed before approval.

stages.name: approval
stages._comment: CEO approves the plan. A plan is dearer than code: one wrong assumption is copied into every task below it.

stages.name: breakdown
stages._comment: Spec with testable acceptance criteria, then task files written into tasks/backlog/. A spec that is not sliced into tasks is half done.
